analytical_allocation_scope: Exact NumPy payload arithmetic under explicit shape/failstop bounds; Python allocator, tskit and library reserve allowances are conservative operational budgets, not a mathematical process RSS proof.
fixed_order_timing_limit: One original/candidate episode pair, separated from reconstruction and archived-hash timing. Measures whole episode stage only; does not causally attribute production GIL or estimate campaign throughput.
guard: Two-second own-process RSS/PSS sampling; own worker exits86 after writing immutable failure metadata on operating limit/error/wall/output failure. No subprocesses allowed. ROOT guardian retains outer32GiB family admission and actual wait/reap. Sampled stop is not an OS quota.
lifetime: Allocate three final input arrays once; stream one unchanged native_tree and unchanged layout at a time; no all-tree list or concatenate duplicate.
Authenticate source tree and roster/sample mapping, then require all three archived structural hashes before either episode builder.
Delete source tree, nodes_time, rank/stamp workspace and loaded table copies before episode timing.
Original builder returns six arrays plus metadata; hash all arrays and inputs, retain only hashes and full plain metadata, delete every output array, collect before candidate.
Candidate uses same three inputs and original unchanged eight-GiB episode payload cap. No two full episode-output sets coexist.
Original _sha copies are included; archived comparison uses streaming framed hashes and does not retain bytes copies.
root_count_guard: Reject whole comparison above 1,048,576 native roots before builders, bounding Python root-partition containers. No topology truncation or ignored holds.
scope: CPU-only episode qualification; no observed genotype, private truth, checkpoint or full observation features read; no native inference or learned/model/optimizer call.
tree_count_guard: Reject whole comparison above 65,536 nodes in any hold; complete-parent hashes still authenticate all arrays before either builder.
